subject: MAP: MediCore evaluation & go-live window — procurement hold and timeline options
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medicore.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: MediCore evaluation & go-live window — procurement hold and timeline options

Alex — attaching the updated MAP and the latest SOW draft after our scoping call. Key points up front: 

- Core evaluation plan remains the same (pilot with 3 departments, perf tests week 3).
- Risk: Procurement indicated a legal review that may delay DocuSign by 10–14 business days.
- If DocuSign slips beyond 4/30 we lose the current deploy window for May P1 cutover.

Requested from your side: please confirm the procurement blocker details and whether your legal team can run an expedited review. From our side I’ve listed mitigation options below — Marcus can weigh technical feasibility.

Attachments: [Attachment: MediCore_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)], [Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf, 92KB)]

Next steps I propose: 
1) You confirm procurement hold specifics by EOD 4/18.
2) If hold is >7 business days, we propose a scoped canary launch (reduced throughput) for the May window and a revised full go-live in early June.
3) If you want us to start expedited playbook (reduced scope + temporary rate limits), Marcus and I can prepare technical constraints by 4/19.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Redwood Inference | Production-first inference platform

From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medicore.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medicore.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medicore.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: MediCore evaluation & go-live window — procurement hold and timeline options

Stephanie — thanks for the MAP and SOW. Quick update from our side:

- Procurement flagged two items in the SOW (data residency clause and indemnity language). Legal asked for a 10 business-day review; procurement added a queue estimate of 2–3 business days on top.
- I don’t expect DocuSign before 4/29 at the earliest; conservative estimate is 5/7.

We’re open to the canary approach if that limits exposure to legal risk and gives us some runway for the evaluation. Questions: 
- What does a "scoped canary" mean operationally (throughput/headroom limits)?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood can start provisioning infra prior to signature if we sign an internal purchase order? Procurement is resistant but willing to consider an LOI for limited pre-provisioning.

Attaching procurement note they shared.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Carter
Director, Product Management | MediCore Health
alex.carter@medicore.com
[Attachment: Procurement_Hold_Note.pdf (pdf, 22KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: MediCore evaluation & go-live window — procurement hold and timeline options

Internal note / technical read:

Stephanie / Laura — read the procurement note. Feasible mitigations we can offer with minimal engineering lift: 

1) Scoped canary (low-risk path): provision a single dedicated instance (1x A10 equivalent), limit to 10 qps, restrict to test accounts + 1 production team. This requires a temporary exception in the MAP: reduced acceptance criteria for throughput and a deferred completion metric for full latency SLA.

2) Feature-flagged rollout: we can gate new capabilities (inference caching, KV pre-warm) behind feature flags so if anything looks off during the canary we can throttle without re-deploy.

3) Pre-provisioning on an LOI: operationally doable, but we need approval from finance to accept LOI terms that cover infrastructure costs (we can cap fees and apply as credit post-signature). Legal will also need to sign a short pre-provisioning addendum — Laura can take point.

Estimate: 3–4 engineering hours to stand up the canary infra and 1 hour for the feature-flag plan. No model re-architecture required.

If we pursue option (1) I can draft a one-page operational exception for the MAP that the customer signs and we attach to the MAP document.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medicore.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@medicore.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: MediCore evaluation & go-live window — procurement hold and timeline options

Alex / Elaine — quick synthesis and proposed path forward: 

Summary of constraints:
- Procurement legal review likely pushes DocuSign to ~5/7 (per your estimate).
- That timeline threatens the May P1 cutover but still allows a limited May pilot if we adopt a scoped canary.

Proposed three-track approach (pick one):
A) Canopy Canary (recommended): Redwood provisions canary infra on LOI basis (cap costs, refundable credit on signature). Launch limited pilot May 10–14. Acceptance: functional checks only (no throughput SLA).
B) Wait & Full Launch: do not provision until DocuSign completes; full go-live targeted for the first week of June (6/7–6/11).
C) Hybrid: Begin pre-provisioning for non-production (engineering-only) immediately, then expand to canary on LOI if procurement agrees.

Action items: 
- Alex: confirm which option you prefer by EOD 4/20. If LOI option (A or C), copy procurement on the LOI terms they can accept.
- Laura: I’ll need a short pre-provisioning addendum template and LOI draft for costs.
- Marcus: draft the one-page operational exception and the feature-flag playbook.

Escalation note: if procurement cannot accept LOI or expedited review, we will need a formal exec escalation to approve a one-time credit for delayed acceptance (I can draft the executive ask and send to our rev ops/leadership).

Attachments: [Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf, 92KB)]

Thanks all — want to keep momentum and avoid a reactive scramble.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medicore.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medicore.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medicore.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: MediCore evaluation & go-live window — procurement hold and timeline options

Stephanie — we’ll go with option A (Canopy Canary) provided procurement can sign an LOI that limits our liability and confirms refundable credit on final signature. Procurement (cc’d) — can you confirm acceptable LOI language today? If not possible, we will pivot to option B and target early June.

Appreciate the clarity and the rapid playbook — Marcus, if you can send the one-pager and a short runbook by EOD that would help my legal/procurement briefing.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Product Management | MediCore Health
alex.carter@medicore.com
